first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A well-researched guide to getting married in Portugal, with regions, airports and legal steps. There is some kind of advisor service behind it, but in the first screen I can't tell if this is a full service destination wedding planner, a venue-finding service or a travel guide. The hero reads like a list of facts about Portugal, not about the firm.

attention_map.quote: Foreign couples start the legal process for a wedding in Portugal at least one month before the date.
attention_map.why: Four separate fact sentences about Portugal. Useful, but nothing tells me who you are or that you do the whole thing for us. The one line that matters to me, 'plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance', is buried in bold under three buttons.

attention_map.quote: Which season suits you? How many guests? What are you celebrating?
attention_map.why: Too early. I haven't decided you're worth contacting yet.

attention_map.quote: Legal and travel details from official sources, including IRN, GOV.UK and Smartraveller.
attention_map.why: Good that GOV.UK is there. Smartraveller means nothing to me as a UK or US couple but it doesn't hurt.

attention_map.section: Fall for Portugal Before You Choose a Venue
attention_map.quote: The legacy of Ferdinand II, the King-Artist
attention_map.why: Pretty, but tourist-brochure. I'm comparing planners, not reading about palaces.
This is what I want: each region tied to an airport. But no driving times from the airport to the venues, except Lisbon later on.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra; nothing may be fixed to the heritage. We check the terms with you before you book.
attention_map.why: This is specific, honest detail. It's the first time the page sounds like it knows the ground.

attention_map.section: See Why Couples Marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: a destination wedding in Portugal gives couples five things in one country.
attention_map.why: Repeats what I just read in the region cards. I'm already sold on Portugal; I need to be sold on you.

attention_map.section: What Your Wedded Advisor Checks in Every Venue Contract
attention_map.quote: VAT: whether each quote includes VAT, so totals compare like for like.
attention_map.why: Shows care with money. But it's about venue pricing, not your fee.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding, Step by Step: Getting There
attention_map.quote: Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre, as a guide; we confirm the transfer time for each venue.
attention_map.why: Close to my 'within two hours of an airport' question, but it's city centre, not airport, and only for Lisbon.

attention_map.section: Entry Rules and Marrying Legally, by Passport
attention_map.quote: The US Embassy in Lisbon does not issue a CNI, because no US authority exists to issue one.
attention_map.why: Genuinely useful and US and UK are covered first, not just Australia. Long, though, and it's the kind of thing I'd expect a planner to handle for me rather than explain.

attention_map.section: What a Wedding in Portugal Costs
attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use. We talk you through the options for your plans.
attention_map.why: A heading promising cost, then no numbers, no fee structure, no currency. Feels like dodging.

attention_map.section: See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package: every weekend is built to your plan.
attention_map.why: Closest thing to scope on the page. The list is the wedding weekend, not what your team does. 'An on-the-day coordinator' sounds like one person on the day, not end-to-end planning.

attention_map.section: Bring Your Guests, or Keep It Exclusive to You
attention_map.quote: Build a guest website in Wonderland Studio: share the schedule, travel and entry rules in one place. Start for free
attention_map.why: 'Start for free' makes this feel like a DIY wedding platform. That's the opposite of the high-touch planner I'm looking for.

attention_map.section: Celebrate More Than a Wedding in Portugal
attention_map.why: Not for me. Dilutes the sense that you specialise in weddings like ours.

attention_map.section: Plan Your Portugal Wedding with One Wedded Advisor
attention_map.quote: Your advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue.
attention_map.why: One contact is what I want. But no name, no face, no experience, no mention of how quickly they reply or how senior they are. The image is just 'wedded-advisor-planning-with-couple'.

attention_map.quote: When you plan with Wedded Concierge, your advisor explains what the programme offers for your dates.

attention_map.why: Form is fine, but 'will reply' with no timeframe. I'm used to fast, senior replies.

attention_map.quote: 4. How Much Is an Average Wedding in Portugal? There is no single average
attention_map.why: Second time the cost question is asked and not answered.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links where I wanted to see your own weddings. Cheapens it.

questions_answered.question: What exactly does end-to-end include?
questions_answered.evidence: 'plans with you from the first enquiry to the last dance', 'Together you shortlist venues and plan the weekend around your guests', and the weekend list ending 'An on-the-day coordinator'. It never says who books suppliers, manages contracts and payments, runs guest travel, or handles design. Reads more like advising and shortlisting than full service.

questions_answered.question: Why an Australian company for a wedding in Europe?
questions_answered.evidence: Nothing explains who Wedded Wonderland is, where it is based or why it is right for a Portugal wedding. The Smartraveller and 'Embassy of Portugal in Canberra' references hint at Australia without explaining it.

questions_answered.question: How far is it from a major airport?
questions_answered.evidence: Every region names its airport, e.g. 'Nearest airport: Faro (FAO)', and 'Many Lisbon-area venues are 15 to 30 minutes from the city centre'. No airport-to-venue times for the Algarve, Douro, Comporta or Madeira.

questions_answered.question: How are fees and supplier costs structured, and in what currency?
questions_answered.evidence: 'What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things' and 'There is no single average'. The venue contract checklist covers venue pricing and VAT, but there is no planner fee, no structure, no ballpark and no currency anywhere.

questions_answered.question: Can we see weddings you have done here?
questions_answered.evidence: No real weddings, testimonials or portfolio. The only wedding links are celebrity ones in 'Trending row' and an unexplained 'A Madeira wedding story'.

trust_signals_noticed: Official sources named and linked: GOV.UK, US Department of State, IRN, Justica
Specific, honest venue caveats: Monserrate roof works to Q1 2027, state events can cancel Queluz bookings
Venue contract checklist including VAT and buy-out fees
US and UK passports covered before Australian

No senior planner names or faces
'Start for free' feels like a self-serve product
Celebrity wedding links in place of own work

emotional_response.overall: Respect for the homework, but no warmth and no sense of who would be looking after us.
emotional_response.emotionally_invested_planner: Not felt. The tone is careful and factual, like a well-written guidebook. Nothing suggests a person who cares about our day.
emotional_response.details_perfect: The legal and venue detail is reassuring; it suggests rigour.

payload.decision_reason: Scope, proof and fees are all unclear and nothing makes the firm feel senior. The legal detail is impressive, but I'm comparing full service planners, and this reads like a Portugal guide with an advisor attached. No planner name, no real weddings, no fee structure or currency. The firms in my other tabs that show those will get my enquiry.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly, this is a really good Portugal guide. I learned things about the CNI I didn't know. But I'm not looking for a guide, I'm looking for the person who'll run our wedding. Who is my planner? Have you done a wedding at a quinta in the Douro? What do you charge, and is that in pounds, dollars or what? It says 'What a Wedding in Portugal Costs' and then doesn't tell me. Then there's 'Start for free' and a list of Ronaldo wedding links, and it starts to feel like a wedding platform, not a full service firm. I'll close the tab.
